chapter: Dancing schools and Charlie Johnson in New York
title: Hired by Charlie Johnson after the McRae Brothers
summary: Charlie Johnson heard the McRae Brothers in Atlantic City and called McRae back to New York in January 1929, after a missed meeting at the station.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How about Charlie Johnson's Band? Did you play with that band?
I played with Charlie Johnson, yeah, after -- I think I played with Charlie Johnson before, after I left my brother. That's when I think I got with Charlie. I went back home to Philly for a while.
And Charlie Johnson had heard me with my brother's band. See, Charlie Johnson always played Atlantic City too, every year. He came over to listen

He used to say, "Aw, man, you guys got a really good band," you know. And Charlie Taylor, violin player, he's out to Egg Harbor. He had a great big band. And he had a beautiful band too (inaudible) Chicago.
They used to come over at night and stand back in the back and listen to us play. He say, "Hey," you know, "you cats got a beautiful band," you know.
And Charlie knew of me then. When Charlie found out we had played, he say, "What happened to McRae Brothers, are they in town?" He say, "Where's the one that plays tenor?"
So he -- say, "He went home." So they called the union in Philly, and they got my address and Charlie Johnson called me up to come back to New York that winter. That was still in 1929.
It was the winter of '29. It was like January. It was cold. It was really a cold winter that year. And I came over and he was supposed to meet

me at the train station. And I waited and I waited and he didn't meet me.
So I got on the train and went on back to Philly.
See, I didn't think to call him up and say come. (Inaudible) I say, 'Oh heck, I'm not -- these guys don't want me. I'm going back to Philly.'

When I got back to Philly, he called me. He say, 'Where you at?' I say, 'I'm home.' 'Will you come on back, we're waiting for you?' So the next day I came back, and I worked over at 5th Avenue, that club that Ed Small had over there for about a couple of months.
